# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Cost-reduction opportunity (if `cost`/`latency`/`num_messages` is a declared objective,
      run `detect_loop_patterns.py --run-dir $R --tag $BEST --split val` — free, no extra
      eval — and check its `by_tool` map for a same-tool-called-N-times-in-a-row pattern. A
      hit names the exact tool + repeat count: propose a composite/bulk tool (capability
      `tools`), a bundled script entrypoint (`skills-package`), or upfront-batched
      instructions (`prompt`/`system-prompt`) that replace the N calls with one. No hit
      (or cost/latency not a declared objective): say so plainly, do not leave this blank):
    - Focus next iteration:

<!-- cap-evolve:journal-append-below — add your Iteration entry under this line; do not edit anything above it -->

## Iteration cand_0001 — Fix action-stall + incomplete reservation enumeration (seed → first candidate)
- Changes I made:
  - policy.md: added "## How to complete a task (READ FIRST)" — execution contract (a task is done only after the write tool RETURNS; on user "yes" the very next turn MUST be the write call, no re-summary/second confirmation) + worked example. Cluster A.
  - policy.md: same section — "look up on-file data before asking" (don't re-ask the account holder's DOB etc.) and "present options & proceed when a referenced record can't be found after checking ALL reservations + flight DB". Cluster C. Plus a softness/judgement clause.
  - tools.py: NEW loop tool `get_all_reservation_details(user_id)` — returns EVERY reservation in one call so the agent can't stop early and miss one. Cluster B.
  - tools.py: enriched `book_reservation` docstring — exact price formula, payment-must-equal-total, certificate-consumed-in-full, full worked argument example (per-param slot docs for the mid reader). Cluster D.
- Expected effect + why safe:
  - A (dominant): on task 8 the agent got "yes" then USER_STOP with book_reservation NEVER called → DB=0. Forcing the write on confirmation makes the DB actually change. Safe: existing "confirm before write" rule preserved; only the post-"yes" step is sharpened.
  - B: task 8 user had 5 reservations; agent read 4 and missed WUNA5K (gold-read `8_1`, the May-10 ORD→PHL flight). One-call enumeration surfaces WUNA5K → agent can rebook the matching flight number. Safe: additive READ tool, per-id lookup kept.
  - C: removes the DOB re-ask and the "can't match May 10" refusal loop. Safe: no permission broadened.
  - D: helps the mid model build a payment amount equal to the exact total, avoiding the "payment does not add up" rejection across the whole booking class. Safe: docs only.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — this is iteration 1 (LEDGER/RUNMAP/rejected.jsonl all empty; seed baseline only).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still not cracked: wrong-argument writes beyond payment total (baggage allowance math, cabin-change refund/charge direction, modify-flight basic-economy guard) — not observed in this single trace; left as prose rules already in the base policy. If future traces show these failing, consider in-body guards/compute tools.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). If this is rejected, the lever to try next is a composite atomic book-and-confirm write tool for cluster A and in-body computation guards for cluster D.
- Cost-reduction opportunity: cost/latency not a declared objective here (reward_basis = DB + COMMUNICATE). The new loop tool nonetheless collapses the N-per-id get_reservation_details loop into one call. Did not run detect_loop_patterns.py (no cost objective).
- Focus next iteration: verify whether book now fires and the correct flight (same flight number from history) is chosen; if DB still mismatches, inspect the exact expected final reservation.
